slot.brief: Two-population problem (e.g. machines/balls from bags); given test/result probabilities, compute posterior probability the item came from a given source; multi-step Bayes.

stem: Factories A and B supply fractions $p$ and $1-p$ of a product. Their defective rates are $\dfrac1{10}$ and $\dfrac15$, respectively. If the overall defective probability is $\dfrac18$, find the probability a defective item came from A.

verdicts.working: Solve p/10 + (1-p)/5 = 1/8, giving p = 3/4. Then P(A | defective) = (p/10)/(1/8) = 3/5.

working:
$\dfrac{p}{10}+\dfrac{1-p}{5}=\dfrac18\Rightarrow p=\dfrac34$
$P(A\mid D)=\dfrac{P(A)P(D\mid A)}{P(D)}=\dfrac{(\frac34)(\frac1{10})}{\frac18}=\dfrac35$

Independent check: Solve p/10 + (1-p)/5 = 1/8, giving p = 3/4. Then P(A | defective) = (p/10)/(1/8) = 3/5.
solution:
By the law of total probability, $p/10+(1-p)/5=1/8$, giving $p=3/4$.
Using Bayes’ theorem,
$$P(A\mid D)=\frac{pP(D\mid A)}{P(D)}=\frac{(3/4)(1/10)}{1/8}=\frac35.$$
